lots.guide_summary: All 10 surviving entries are SOLD hammers at Gowans, Hobart (AUD, premium extra, no conversion). The three closest (halo or cluster style) made $110 to $330; plain 9ct white-stone rings of other styles made $50 to $310. No UNSOLD or ASKING evidence; WebSearch was capped, so no Armitage past results.
lots.working: Keep: lowest close same-item SOLD = $110 (Gowans 414444, June 2026). $110 / 1.22 = $90.16, round down to $90. Flip: likely resale about $200 hammer (middle of the close $110 to $330 range). Less 20% seller commission incl GST if re-offered at a Tasmanian auction, no postage (local) = $160. $160 / 2.44 = $65.57, round down to $65. All comps within 24 months.
lots.confidence_reason: Single photo, no hallmark readable (9ct is Armitage's word only), stones not identified (diamond versus paste changes value a lot), and comps are close in style, not the same ring.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped the researcher's aggregate entry '$150 to $260 hammer (several)' with aud_price 200: it is a summary of many sales, not a single price. Reclassified 401386 ($310) and 401380 ($150) from close to category guide after checking photos (both are solitaires, not clusters). Researcher's URLs were search queries; replaced with the individual lot API URLs, which I opened.
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged crop shows a round pale yellow-green centre stone (could be a yellowish diamond, citrine, peridot or CZ) in a halo of roughly 12 small white stones in a white-metal setting, yellow gold band with engraved scroll or leaf shoulders. No hallmark visible. Band looks intact, no obvious missing stones in the halo from this angle.
lots.condition: Appears complete and wearable from the one photo; wear, size, weight and stone security unknown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is the ring hallmarked 9ct (or 375), what does it weigh and what size is it? Have the stones been tested, are the halo stones diamonds or paste, and are any stones chipped or loose?
